transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Havenbridge - Head of ML Ops), Sofia Reyes (Havenbridge - CTO), Ethan Mills (Havenbridge - Infra)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on cost/unit economics for Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; touched on batching/caching levers, expected token volumes, and security/VPC requirements. Agreed next steps: pricing spreadsheet, benchmark script, technical deep dive.

Topics:
- Per-token pricing vs unit economics for dedicated pools
- Batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization as cost levers
- Commitment sizing and burst traffic handling for Dedicated
- Security/compliance: SOC2, KMS, VPC, SSO

Transcript:
[00:00] Maria Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Um, quick intros — I'm Maria, AE on the account, and Devon here is our SE.
[00:08] Devon Park: hi all, Devon Park, infra/latency nerd at Redwood.
[00:11] Liam O'Connor: Liam O'Connor, I run ML Ops at Havenbridge. Sofia and Ethan are with me.
[00:15] Sofia Reyes: hey.
[00:16] Ethan Mills: afternoon.
[00:18] Maria Chen: Awesome. So today we want to focus on cost economics — per-token pricing, how batching and caching change unit costs, and the tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Liam, can you give us a quick sense of your current workload?
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: Sure. We're building a document summarization + Q&A product for internal research analysts. Roughly 20M tokens per month right now, spike to 60M during earnings weeks, um, and our latency SLO is around 300-500ms p50 for summaries, tighter for short Q&A. We're evaluating whether to keep on hosted APIs or move to dedicated GPUs to lower cost.
[00:52] Devon Park: Got it. Quick clarifying q — are those tokens counted pre-or post-truncation? Like full context or trimmed?
[00:56] Liam O'Connor: pre, so includes the full doc context, which is why we've got long seqs sometimes — 1k to 6k tokens.
[01:02] Maria Chen: That matters a lot for batching and KV cache efficiency. Ok, from a pricing lens, our hosted offering has per-token pricing with model tiers. Example numbers we gave in the deck: for a medium open model hosted, you're looking at order-of-magnitude X per 1k tokens for gen, embeddings are separate. For Dedicated, the unit cost is lower when you amortize GPU hours across steady throughput — you're effectively buying reserved capacity and paying a monthly commit plus infra.
[01:24] Sofia Reyes: can you be more concrete? our CFO wants back-of-envelope numbers today.
[01:28] Maria Chen: Yeah, sure. So to be explicit — for hosted gen calls on our open-medium model, think of it as roughly $0.15-$0.30 per 1k tokens depending on SLA and model family. On Dedicated, if you commit to a 3-6 month reserved pool sized for your p95 traffic, your effective per-1k-token cost can drop to the low cents or even sub-cent level when you're fully utilizing GPU hours and using batching/caching. Those are illustrative; we'll send a detailed spreadsheet.
[01:58] Ethan Mills: ok that range helps. how much of that delta comes from batching vs just static reserved pricing?
[02:04] Devon Park: Good Q. It's both. Reserved capacity reduces the marginal compute price because you're not paying per-request overhead, but batching and caching are multiplicative savings. For example, continuous batching on our runtime can pack multiple concurrent requests into one kernel run — for short prompts that saves tokens and GPU time. Prefix/KV cache helps a lot for long-context workflows because repeated doc prefixes don't require recomputation. Together, typical customers see 20-60% reduction in per-token cost just from batching + caching depending on request pattern.
[02:36] Maria Chen: And additional levers include quantization model variants — moving from fp16 to int8/int4 variants reduces memory and allows denser packing on a GPU, which helps in Dedicated.
[02:44] Liam O'Connor: Do you support automatic fallbacks if we use quantized models and quality drops? Like, we want safety net for accuracy regressions.
[02:50] Devon Park: Yeah — we have rollout controls and auto-fallbacks. You can set canary rules or quality thresholds tied to evals and Redwood will route to the next compatible variant. We'll also keep token-level tracing so you can correlate quality vs model variant.
[03:02] Sofia Reyes: What about burst? We have earnings week spikes, as I said. If we go Dedicated and it saturates, is there an easy burst-to-hosted path?
[03:10] Maria Chen: We offer burst capacity: Dedicated customers can configure a burst policy that automatically routes excess requests to hosted capacity (with clear pricing for burst). There are also multi-region fallback routes.
[03:19] Ethan Mills: Are there egress costs if you burst to hosted? We have strict cloud cost accounting.
[03:23] Maria Chen: Good point — egress depends on your deployment topology. If you're on Dedicated in our cloud, intra-region egress is minimal. For Private/VPC, egress to hosted is a consideration; we'll surface that in the deep dive.
[03:33] Liam O'Connor: Security notes — we need SOC2, KMS integration, and audit logs. Also SSO.
[03:38] Devon Park: Yep. Redwood has SOC2 Type II, SAML/SSO, and KMS support (customer-managed keys for private deployments). Audit logs and token-level tracing are standard on Dedicated/Private. We'll attach our security whitepaper.
[03:48] Maria Chen: We'll send the SOC2 and network diagrams. Link here for SOC2 summary: https://redwood.docs/security/soc2 (placeholder).
[03:55] Sofia Reyes: for Private (VPC or on-prem), what's the uplift? i.e., how much more do we pay for Private vs Dedicated?
[04:02] Maria Chen: Private includes the platform fee and support, plus infra costs. Rough rule of thumb: Private is higher fixed cost but gives you control for compliance. Detailed numbers depend on region and whether on-prem. We'll include scenarios in the pricing sheet.
[04:13] Liam O'Connor: Ok, back to unit economics: If we give you our token exports and expected SLOs, can you run a benchmark to show a modeled monthly cost across Hosted/Dedicated/Private?
[04:22] Devon Park: Absolutely — we can run perf scripts against a set of model variants. We'll need a sample of input distributions (prompt length, response length, concurrency). We have a bench script we can share; we can run it in our lab against open models and return token cost projections.
[04:33] Maria Chen: We'll share two artifacts: 1) pricing spreadsheet with hosted vs dedicated vs private scenarios, and 2) benchmark script and instructions + a sample results sheet. Links we'll send: pricing sheet (private link) and bench spreadsheet (placeholder): https://redwood.storage/bench/havenbridge.xlsx
[04:48] Ethan Mills: Sounds good. Who owns the benchmark run? you run it or we run in our environment?
[04:53] Devon Park: We can do both. We can run a controlled run in our infra to show the delta and provide the script so you can run it in your VPC/Private environment for apples-to-apples numbers.
[05:02] Liam O'Connor: Great. Anything else on cost levers we should know?
[05:06] Devon Park: A couple practical notes — 1) prefix caching is most effective when you have repeated doc contexts (like summaries over the same corpora). 2) Batching has latency tradeoffs; if you need strict p50 latency you tune batch windows conservatively. 3) Model selection matters — sometimes switching to a smaller family with good prompting buys outsized savings. 4) Embeddings and reranking pipelines are often the bulk of tokens for search workflows so treat them separately in the model mix.
[05:33] Sofia Reyes: One more — can Redwood expose per-route cost analytics so our product teams can see per-feature economics?
[05:39] Maria Chen: Yes — Console gives per-route token and cost breakdowns, and you can set rate limits and quotas.
[05:44] Ethan Mills: ok good.
[05:46] Maria Chen: Quick recap of next steps: we'll send the pricing spreadsheet and benchmark script; Devon will schedule a technical deep dive to validate VPC/egress and run a bench; Havenbridge to share token exports and SLOs. Any other asks?
[05:59] Liam O'Connor: please include an example invoice or two for hosted and an example committed plan for Dedicated so our finance team can model it.
[06:06] Maria Chen: Will do.
[06:07] Sofia Reyes: and security docs.
[06:08] Devon Park: I'll include the SOC2 snapshot and KMS integration guide.
[06:11] Maria Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with notes and links.
[06:15] Liam O'Connor: thanks all.
[06:17] Sofia Reyes: bye.
[06:18] Ethan Mills: bye.

End of transcript.
